questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L06 Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Slide note: Source checks prevent weak evidence. Which speaker note best supports it? \

answer.text: A. Checking author, date, and purpose helps students decide whether evidence is reliable enough to use.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains the slide and connects it to the presentation purpose.

answer.text: B. Source checks prevent weak evidence because source checks prevent weak evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This repeats the slide without explaining it.

answer.text: C. I will read the slide exactly as written.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reading the slide does not add oral explanation.

answer.text: D. The slide is about something from school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and does not explain the slide.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L06 Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Which slide note is strongest for integrated communication? \

answer.text: A. A full paragraph of speaker notes

feedback.text: Incorrect. Slides should not carry the entire speech.

answer.text: B. Things about writing and stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and not presentation-ready.

answer.text: C. I will explain this later maybe

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not communicate a clear idea.

answer.text: D. Revision improves clarity and cohesion.

feedback.text: Correct. This note is concise and gives the audience a clear anchor.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.03 U06 L06 Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03 In this lesson, what does "integrated" mean? \

answer.text: A. unrelated and separate

feedback.text: Incorrect. Integrated means parts work together, not separately.

answer.text: B. decorative and colorful

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration is not the meaning of integrated.

answer.text: C. combined so the parts work together

feedback.text: Correct. Oral explanation and digital slides should work together.

answer.text: D. confusing and crowded

feedback.text: Incorrect. Integrated communication should be clear, not crowded.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.L.01 U06 L06 Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Which speaker note uses standard English? \

answer.text: A. Slide notes helps audiences follow ideas.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The verb does not agree with the plural subject.

answer.text: B. Slide notes helping audiences follow ideas.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Slide note help audience follows ideas.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This has multiple agreement errors.

answer.text: D. Slide notes help audiences follow ideas.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence uses standard English agreement.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.03 U06 L06 Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.03 What makes a collaborative digital presentation publication-ready? \

answer.text: A. Clear wording, consistent formatting, and audience-aware content

feedback.text: Correct. These qualities help a presentation be ready to share.

answer.text: B. Random formatting and unclear slide notes

feedback.text: Incorrect. These would weaken publication quality.

answer.text: C. Unchecked spelling and missing audience focus

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication-ready work should be polished.

answer.text: D. Crowded slides with unrelated paragraphs

feedback.text: Incorrect. Crowded, unrelated slides are not publication-ready.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L06 Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Which speaker behavior best supports digital slides? \

answer.text: A. Read every slide word for word and add nothing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Oral delivery should explain, not merely repeat.

answer.text: B. Explain the meaning of each concise slide note.

feedback.text: Correct. This helps the audience understand how the slide supports the message.

answer.text: C. Ignore the slides completely.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Integrated communication requires connection between slides and speaking.

answer.text: D. Talk about unrelated details while slides appear.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would confuse the audience. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L06 Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Which digital slide is most effective? \

answer.text: A. A concise note: "Feedback reveals unclear claims."

feedback.text: Correct. This note is short and connected to a clear idea.

answer.text: B. A paragraph with six full sentences

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is likely too crowded for a slide.

answer.text: C. A vague label that says "stuff"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not guide the audience. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. An unrelated picture with no caption

feedback.text: Incorrect. This would not support coherent ideas.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.03 U06 L06 Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03 The phrase "publication-ready" most nearly means what? \

answer.text: A. impossible to revise

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication-ready work usually becomes stronger through revision.

answer.text: B. unfinished and full of placeholders

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication-ready work should not be unfinished.

answer.text: C. polished enough to share with the intended audience

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. unrelated to any audience

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication-ready work should be tailored to an audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L06 Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Slide note: "Check author, date, purpose." Which oral explanation is best? \

answer.text: A. I put three words on the slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain why the checks matter.

answer.text: B. The slide is short, so I do not need to say anything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A short slide still needs oral explanation.

answer.text: C. Author, date, and purpose are words.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support the presentation purpose.

answer.text: D. These three checks help students decide whether a source is trustworthy and useful for research.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains the slide's meaning. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.L.01 U06 L06 Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.03 Which slide note is conventionally correct? \

answer.text: A. Feedback improve writing clarity.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The verb does not agree with the subject.

answer.text: B. Feedback improves writing clarity.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Feedback improving writing clarity.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Feedback improve writing's clarity's.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This contains agreement and apostrophe errors.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L06 Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Which pairing works best? \

answer.text: A. Slide: "Revision improves clarity." Speaker: "Lunch schedules are confusing."

feedback.text: Incorrect. The speaker note is unrelated. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Slide: "Revision improves clarity." Speaker: "Revision improves clarity."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only repeats the slide. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Slide: "Revision improves clarity." Speaker: "Revision helps readers follow ideas because writers can strengthen wording and transitions."

feedback.text: Correct. The speaker note explains the slide without simply repeating it.

answer.text: D. Slide: "Revision improves clarity." Speaker: "Look at this slide silently."

feedback.text: Incorrect. The speaker should explain the slide.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.03 U06 L06 Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Which word has the strongest positive connotation for a presentation product? \

answer.text: A. polished

feedback.text: Correct. Polished suggests careful revision and presentation-ready quality.

answer.text: B. unfinished

feedback.text: Incorrect. This suggests the work is not ready.

answer.text: C. sloppy

feedback.text: Incorrect. This has a negative connotation. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. random

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random suggests lack of organization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.03 U06 L06 Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03 In collaborative publication work, why should students review formatting consistency? \

answer.text: A. Consistency makes the content less clear.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Consistency usually supports clarity.

answer.text: B. Consistent formatting helps the final product look organized and audience-ready.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Formatting should be random in published work.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random formatting weakens polish. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Formatting replaces the need for clear ideas.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Formatting supports, but does not replace, content.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L06 Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Which speaker note best avoids simply reading the slide? \

answer.text: A. My slide says feedback reveals unclear claims.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This mostly repeats the slide. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Feedback reveals unclear claims, feedback reveals unclear claims.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This repeats the slide. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. I will not explain this slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The speaker should explain the slide.

answer.text: D. Feedback reveals unclear claims because readers can point out where the writer's idea needs more explanation.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L06 Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.03 A slide says, "Source credibility." What is the best revision? \

answer.text: A. Source credibility and all the many things that could happen with sources

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is wordy and unclear. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Stuff about whether sources are things

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and confusing. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Check source credibility before using evidence.

feedback.text: Correct. This revision is clear, concise, and action-oriented.

answer.text: D. Credibility source maybe use

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is unclear and not publication-ready.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.L.01 U06 L06 Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Which sentence should be revised before publication? \

answer.text: A. Slide notes helps the audience understand the focus.

feedback.text: Correct. The verb should be "help" because the subject "notes" is plural.

answer.text: B. Speaker notes explain the slide in more detail.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sentence is correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Clear slides help audiences follow the message.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sentence is correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Publication-ready work uses standard English.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sentence is correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.03 U06 L06 Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 In the sentence "The slide is crowded," what does "crowded" suggest? \

answer.text: A. The slide is reliable.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Crowded does not mean reliable. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. The slide has a clear focus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Crowded often suggests the opposite.

answer.text: C. The slide has too much information or too many elements.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. The slide is empty.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Crowded means too full, not empty.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.03 U06 L06 Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03 Which final check best supports publication-ready collaborative work? \

answer.text: A. Confirm that slide titles, wording, and formatting are clear and consistent.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Add unrelated text from every group member.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unrelated text weakens the final product.

answer.text: C. Leave spelling unchecked.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication-ready work should be edited.

answer.text: D. Remove the audience focus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Audience focus is necessary for publication quality.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L06 Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Which statement best describes integration? \

answer.text: A. The slides should contain every spoken word.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would overload slides and reduce oral value.

answer.text: B. The speaker and slides should communicate connected parts of the same message.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. The speaker should ignore the slides.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would separate the parts. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. The speaker should change topics while slides stay the same.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would confuse the audience. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L06 Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.03 Which slide note is most concise? \

answer.text: A. Writing and revising and readers and all that stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and vague. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Revision is something that can maybe help people who read things in some ways.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too wordy and vague. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. The thing about revision is that it is a thing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unclear and circular. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. Revision helps readers.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.03 U06 L06 Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 What is the denotative meaning of "audience" in this lesson? \

answer.text: A. the title of a slide

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title is not the audience. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. the color of a presentation

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color is a design choice, not the audience.

answer.text: C. the file name of a document

feedback.text: Incorrect. A file name is not the audience. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. the people who receive or view the communication

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L06 Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Which speaker note best matches the slide note "Evidence supports perspective"? \

answer.text: A. Evidence supports perspective; evidence supports perspective.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This repeats without explaining. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. Evidence supports the perspective by giving the audience a reason to trust the claim.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. This slide is blue and white.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the idea. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: D. I am done with this slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.03 U06 L06 Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03 Which collaborative action is most appropriate before sharing a final presentation? \

answer.text: A. The group reviews the full presentation for audience fit, conventions, and consistent formatting.

feedback.text: Correct. This supports publication-ready quality.

answer.text: B. Each group member checks only their own slide and ignores the whole presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The final product needs whole-presentation consistency.

answer.text: C. The group adds unrelated content to make it longer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length does not improve publication quality.

answer.text: D. The group removes all speaker notes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Speaker notes support oral communication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.L.01 U06 L06 Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Which revision fixes the convention error? Original: "The slides supports the speaker." \

answer.text: A. The slides supporting the speaker.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. The slide supports the speakers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This changes the meaning and does not keep the plural slide idea.

answer.text: C. The slides support the speaker.

feedback.text: Correct. The plural subject "slides" needs the verb "support."

answer.text: D. The slides supports speaker's.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This keeps the agreement error and adds an apostrophe problem.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L06 Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.03 Which final product best integrates oral and digital communication? \

answer.text: A. Crowded slides with no oral explanation

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overloads the audience and weakens delivery.

answer.text: B. Concise slides with speaker notes that explain and extend each slide

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Speaker notes that discuss unrelated topics

feedback.text: Incorrect. Speaker notes must connect to the slides.

answer.text: D. Slides with random images and no clear perspective

feedback.text: Incorrect. This lacks coherent digital communication.
